# claude-runbook-quickref-html — Auto-generated quick-reference HTML card

**Owner**: claude. **Depends on**: existing RUNBOOK at
`docs/skycot/RUNBOOK.md` — read-only consumer.

## Scope

The RUNBOOK is comprehensive but long. Operators on a hot incident need a
one-screen card: top 10 commands + the 5 most common error fixes. This
brief adds a generator script that pulls those sections out of RUNBOOK and
emits a self-contained HTML page.

This is **a build script**, not a runtime feature. Output lives at
`docs/skycot/quickref.html` and is regenerated on demand. No new crate
code; no clippy footprint.

## Approach (concrete)

1. **NEW** `scripts/gen-runbook-quickref.sh` (~120 lines bash):
   - Parses `docs/skycot/RUNBOOK.md` for fenced markers:
     `<!-- quickref:commands:start -->` … `<!-- quickref:commands:end -->`
     `<!-- quickref:errors:start -->` … `<!-- quickref:errors:end -->`
   - Renders to a single self-contained `docs/skycot/quickref.html`
     (inline CSS, no external assets)
   - Stamps generated-at timestamp + source git SHA in a footer
   - Exits non-zero if either marker pair is missing
2. **Modify** `docs/skycot/RUNBOOK.md` — narrow: add the four marker
   comments around the existing top-commands and common-errors blocks.
   Do **not** rewrite the surrounding prose.
3. **NEW** `docs/skycot/quickref.html` (committed output, regenerated by
   the script) — operators can open it directly without running the script.

## Files you may touch

- `scripts/gen-runbook-quickref.sh` (NEW, ≤ 150 LOC)
- `docs/skycot/RUNBOOK.md` — narrow: add 4 marker comments
- `docs/skycot/quickref.html` (NEW, generated, committed)

## Files you must NOT touch

- Any code under `crates/` — this brief is docs+script only
- Other RUNBOOK content — markers only
- CI workflow files — script is on-demand for v1, not CI-enforced

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] `bash scripts/gen-runbook-quickref.sh` produces `docs/skycot/quickref.html`
- [ ] HTML opens cleanly in a browser; no external CSS/JS required
- [ ] Top-commands and common-errors sections both present and styled distinctly
- [ ] Footer shows generated-at UTC + short git SHA
- [ ] Script exits non-zero with a clear message if markers missing
- [ ] Re-running the script produces byte-identical output (deterministic,
      apart from the timestamp — pin via `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` if set)
- [ ] Script passes `shellcheck` (`shellcheck -x scripts/gen-runbook-quickref.sh`)

## Branch + PR

- Branch: `claude-runbook-quickref-html`
- PR title: `docs: gen-runbook-quickref.sh + quickref.html (claude-runbook-quickref-html)`

## Notes for the implementer

- Use bash + `awk` for the marker extraction. No Python, no Node — keeps
  the script invocable on a fresh clone with no extra deps.
- HTML scaffold: a single `<style>` block, two `<section>` elements, a
  `<footer>`. Aim for ≤ 200 lines of generated HTML.
- For the SHA, prefer `git rev-parse --short HEAD` with a fallback of
  `unknown` when not in a git checkout.
- `SOURCE_DATE_EPOCH` honoring lets reproducible-build CI lock the
  timestamp. Document the env var in a script header comment.
- Cross-link from RUNBOOK to `quickref.html` so operators discover it.
